text.p: Solid Capital Holdings on Thursday issued a buy recommendation for Koor Industries, saying Israel's largest industrial concern is trading at a 40 percent discount to its holdings.
Solid, which had previously rated Koor a long-term buy, estimated the company's net asset value at $1.99 billion.
Solid set a 12-month price target of $23-$25 for Koor's ADRs traded on the New York Stock Exchange. The shares are trading at $19-1/8.
In 1997 Koor is expected to report a 23 percent decline in operating profits that should be offset to some extent by capital gains from the sale of certain holdings, Solid said in a report.
"The only sector that is expected to report growth in 1997 is the agrochemical sector...and to some extent the food sector," the report said.
Koor will reach a turning point in early 1998 as its electronic and telecommunications sector improve, Solid said.
The infrastructure and building sector will experience a further decline in the second half of 1997 due to a reduction in building starts, the report said.

But in the future total sales are expected to grow moderately due to large scale non-residential projects which require large quantities of cement; increased sales to the Palestinian Authority; and the stabilisation of building starts at a level of around 45,000 a year.
